turns.query: Using SEC MIDAS individual security-by-exchange observations and FINRA consolidated daily short-volume files for April 2025, determine their common trading dates. For cross-source ticker identity, match a MIDAS dot-form share-class ticker to the FINRA symbol obtained by replacing its period separator with a slash; otherwise require exact ticker-string equality. A ticker enters the comparison only if, on every common date, it has at least one MIDAS observation with both trade and odd-lot volume reported and one FINRA row. Report the common-date count and the eligible-ticker count. Carry that population forward and explain what the two sources each cover.

claims.description: The response explains that MIDAS volume reflects on-exchange continuous trading and generally excludes off-exchange, opening and closing auction, and off-hours volume, whereas the FINRA file covers publicly disseminated off-exchange activity reported to FINRA facilities; the two totals therefore have distinct scopes and are not a market-wide accounting reconciliation.

turns.query: Across that full-coverage population, aggregate MIDAS volumes before forming shares and rank tickers by absolute aggregate odd-lot volume, breaking ties alphabetically. Report the ordered top-five cohort, and for the leading ticker its aggregate MIDAS trade volume, odd-lot volume and odd-lot share. Carry the five-ticker cohort forward and explain how the volume level and the share differ as measures.

claims.description: The response treats aggregate odd-lot volume as a level that rises with a ticker's overall activity and the odd-lot share as the scale-free measure of how that activity is composed.

turns.query: Within that five-ticker cohort, rank by aggregate FINRA short volume divided by aggregate FINRA total volume, breaking ties alphabetically. Report that leader, its MIDAS odd-lot-volume rank, odd-lot volume and share, and its FINRA short, short-exempt and total volumes plus short-volume share. Explain how the two leadership measures relate and the limits of combining their interpretations.

claims.description: The response explains that absolute MIDAS odd-lot volume and within-cohort FINRA short-volume share reward different scale and denominator properties, so their leaders need not be the same ticker.
The response identifies FINRA daily short volume as reported transaction volume rather than short interest, an outstanding short position or a direct measure of bearish conviction.
The response explains that FINRA short-exempt volume is the separately reported exempt subset already included in short volume, rather than an additional disjoint volume to add to short volume.

If the response infers retail participation, liquidity, execution quality, sentiment or subsequent returns, it states that the descriptive volume measures and same-month alignment do not establish that interpretation or causality.

judge_reference.source: SEC MIDAS April 2025 individual security-by-exchange observations and FINRA April 2025 consolidated daily short-volume files
facts: There are 21 common trading dates and 6,516 common tickers with observations on every common date in both sources after applying the pinned dot-to-slash share-class bridge. Raw ticker-string equality alone yields 6,502.

The top five by aggregate MIDAS odd-lot volume are NVDA, TSLA, SPY, PLTR and AAPL. NVDA leads with 2.493174923 billion MIDAS trade shares, 0.466144230 billion odd-lot shares and an 18.6968 percent odd-lot share.

PLTR ranks fourth in MIDAS odd-lot volume at 0.194594574 billion shares with a 22.0100 percent odd-lot share, but leads the five-ticker cohort in FINRA short-volume share: 0.738256927 billion ShortVolume, 0.010968187 billion separately reported ShortExemptVolume and 1.237593616 billion TotalVolume, for 59.6526 percent.

FINRA ShortVolume already includes executed short-sale and short-sale-exempt volume; ShortExemptVolume is its separately reported exempt subset and must not be added again. SEC MIDAS volume generally reflects on-exchange continuous trading, while the FINRA consolidated file reflects publicly disseminated off-exchange activity reported to TRFs and the ADF.
known_overclaims: Selecting the cohort by MIDAS trade volume or equal-weighted row ratios instead of aggregate odd-lot volume.
Treating ShortExemptVolume as disjoint from ShortVolume or adding the separately reported subset again to the FINRA numerator.
Treating FINRA short volume as short interest or combining the two source totals as a market-wide accounting identity.
Inferring retail behavior, market quality, sentiment or causality from the descriptive volume relationship.
